lesson.title: Review Day: Fraction Equivalence and Comparison
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: This week you worked with fractions four different ways. Let's review it all!

Quick review: multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number gives an equivalent fraction (Day 1). Dividing them simplifies a fraction (Day 2). A common denominator lets you compare different-denominator fractions (Day 3). A benchmark fraction like 1/2 gives a quick comparison shortcut (Day 4). Simplify 6/8, then use a benchmark to say if the simplified fraction is more or less than 1/2.
Great work this week — you learned to generate, simplify, and compare fractions two different ways! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review generating equivalent fractions, simplifying, and two comparison methods
Simplify a fraction and apply a benchmark comparison to the result
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child simplify 6/8 and compare the result to 1/2.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of real fraction work!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often different-denominator comparison) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child to explain when they'd use the common-denominator method versus the benchmark-fraction shortcut
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four fraction skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: 6/8 simplifies to 3/4. Since 4/8 (or 3/6) would equal 1/2, and 3/4 is greater than 1/2, the simplified fraction 3/4 is more than 1/2.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 4 fraction standards (4.NF.1/4.NF.2) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
